notes: Loop 2 (loop 1: 7.2). Evidence: the 15:06 dry run after commit 2712407 (not re-run, so the parallel judges' evidence stays put). Read SKILL.md (138 lines, was 214), all six references and instructions.ts. Ran classifyQuestion on 33 prompts, the demo analyses and plans, an in-process MCP session (de/pl/en starts, rain, happy hour, German numbers) and my own production-like build: 13 https MCP URLs, no {{ or localhost. Strong: all five loop-1 items handled. Trigger in four languages; the tool backs the near-miss rule (rain, rent, aliens → not_a_decision). Number read-backs; lang on every call. The price dialogue matches the engine (−9.7%, 60 a week, €91.02). Connect steps per app, with PowerShell. Held back: (1) maths.md's by-hand test and log rules, called 'the rule the tools use', contradict decision.ts and the report card (keep 11 / tweak 6–10 / €360 vs keep 7 / tweak 4–6 / €295 cash). (2) 'template: null → near miss' lumps four kinds; happy hour, which the skill calls modelled, comes back unclear. (3) es/pl labels, address form and the German break-even word differ from the report. (4) No 401 path; an empty contact ships 'Ask here: .'.
improvements: Make the by-hand test rule the engine's rule (never-compute criterion; red flag 'instructions that contradict the tool results'). skill/what-if/references/maths.md:261 says 'This is the rule the tools use', but :266-279 keeps the loop-1 rule: keep at break_even (11), tweak 6 to 10, stop below 6, and a stop line of about €360 that includes switching. src/engine/decision.ts:18-25 and experiment.ts:70, and the shipped card (report-en.txt:306-317, report.txt:547-552), give keep from the going-forward break-even (7), tweak 4 to 6, stop below 4, €295 cash by day 5, €410 cash over the whole test, and switching shown separately (about €68 by day 5). coaching.md:174 gives €10.50 as keep 9 / tweak 5-8 / €330; planTest gives keep 6 / tweak 3-5 / payback 9 / €295. maths.md:308 judges a logged result against 'the new break-even (unrounded)', but compare.ts:218-220 applies the card's thresholds. SKILL.md:121 'tied to the break-even' does not say which one. Fix: rewrite both by-hand sections from decision.ts (keepFrom = ongoing break-even rounded up; tweakFrom = max(1, ceil(0.5 × the exact ongoing break-even)); payBackFrom = the test break-even; cash stop line = setup + daily_cost × mid) and fix the demo lines. In SKILL.md step 6, say 'keep from 7 a day; 11 also pays back the test'. Add a check that compares maths.md's demo rule lines with planTest for €9.90 and €10.50. It worked when a by-hand session and /try print the same card.

Branch on `kind`, not on `template: null` (trigger precision). SKILL.md:22 treats every `template: null` as a near miss. whatif_start also returns null for kind 'unsupported' (hiring: that needs the 'not yet' path at SKILL.md:129), 'unclear' and 'results'. SKILL.md:129 and coaching.md:224 say happy hour is a modelled fixed-price offer, and the description promises 'a discount'. Yet classifyQuestion('Was wäre, wenn ich eine Happy Hour mache?'), ('What if I start a happy hour from 4 to 6?') and ('What if I give 10% off to students?') return 'unclear'. The tool then says 'Noch keine Zahlen abfragen … klären, welche Entscheidung ansteht', so the model asks the owner which decision she means right after she named one. The skill's own return phrases, 'Ich habe den Test gemacht', 'Zrobiłam test' and 'Ya hice la prueba' (SKILL.md:21), also classify as 'unclear'. Fix: in step 1 map not_a_decision → near miss; unsupported → 'not yet' and the paper method; unclear but a fixed-price offer or a one-item discount → whatif_check_inputs with lunch_offer / price_change, saying how the fields are used; results → step 7. Ask the mcp owner to cover happy hour, discounts and the three return phrases. Make every example sentence in SKILL.md and coaching.md a test fixture with its expected kind. It worked when each quoted example gets the kind the skill expects.

Use the report's words in all four languages (loop 2 language check). berlin.md:60-72 and coaching.md:21 tell the model to say de 'Gewinnschwelle', es 'su dato' / 'datos de ejemplo' with usted, and pl 'obliczone' / 'wymyślone' / 'dane przykładowe' with Pan/Pani. The shipped report says 'Break-even' in German (report.txt:38 and :282; 'Gewinnschwelle' appears 0 times). In Spanish it says 'Tus datos' and 'Datos de demostración' and uses tú ('puedes comprobar', report-es.txt:48-52). In Polish it says 'Wyliczone', 'Wyobrażone' and 'Dane demonstracyjne' and uses ty ('Twoje liczby', report-pl.txt:44-50). The tool's Polish questions use ty too ('Któremu produktowi chcesz zmienić cenę?'), while coaching.md:39 says to take the tool's ask texts nearly word for word. So the chat names the source labels with words the owner never sees on the chips, and switches the form of address halfway. Fix: build the label table from the report's message catalog, or align the catalogs, and pick one form of address per language for the skill, the tools and the report. Add a check that compares the berlin.md label row with the chip labels. It worked when the chat's label words equal the chips in report-<lang>.txt.

Give the owner a path when the invite code fails. SKILL.md step 0 (lines 67-73) covers only 'whatif_start is not among your tools'. connect.md:183 says 'If it says the code is not valid', but hosts usually treat a 401 without WWW-Authenticate (src/mcp/http.ts:270-279) as a sign-in prompt or a failed connector, so the owner may never see the friendly German/English text. Add one line to step 0 and to connect.md, 'Checking it works': if the app shows the connector as failed, asks you to authenticate, or the tools are missing, open {{SITE_URL}}/api/mcp?code=… in a browser. If it does not say "valid": true, the code or the link is wrong: ask the person who invited you. If a tool call returns the closed-beta error mid-chat, relay it in the owner's language and never repeat the code. It worked when a test session with a wrong code ends with the owner checking her link, not retrying.

Do not ship an empty contact. Leaving WHATIF_BETA_CONTACT unset is allowed (the build only notes 'the site hides the request-a-code button'). My production-like build with WHATIF_SITE_URL=https://what-if-berlin.vercel.app and no contact ships SKILL.md:70 'No invite code yet? Ask here: .' and connect.md:21 'To ask for one: . If no contact is shown there…'. The check skill-zip-prod-url always sets a contact, so it never sees this. Fix: let scripts/build.mjs fill {{BETA_CONTACT}} with a whole sentence ('Ask here: <contact>.' or 'Ask the person who invited you.'), warn on a Vercel build with no contact, and remove the workaround at SKILL.md:73. Run the check once without a contact. It worked when an unset-contact zip has no ': .' in it.

Finish the paths for apps without skills. The connect page the owner actually opens (site/connect.html:156-157, connect-beta.txt) still offers only 'unzip what-if-skill.zip -d ~/.claude/skills/', which fails in a Windows terminal, and its ChatGPT card ends with 'schreiben Sie: Was wäre, wenn …?' with no starter prompt. STARTER_PROMPTS (src/mcp/instructions.ts:56-81) exist in four languages and nothing uses them; only the skill's connect.md:106-144 shows them, and a ChatGPT owner never reads that file. Show the starter prompt for the page's language in the ChatGPT card, and the PowerShell / Explorer steps from connect.md:166-173. Also add a by-hand route for step 5: SKILL.md step 0 and maths.md say nothing about the rehearsal without tools. Say that it needs the tools, or allow a short role-play labelled imagined, with no counts. It worked when a ChatGPT owner can copy the starter prompt from /connect, and a skill-only session never invents rehearsal counts.
